title: Terrorism Frays Morality: The Effects of the 2022 Istanbul Bombing on Moral Foundations, Generosity, and Cooperation
abstract: Terrorism aims to fray the moral fabric of society. We conducted the first preregistered study to assess the impact of real terror threats by combining pre–post comparisons with an experimental threat reminder, examining moral judgments and behaviors of 222 participants before and after the 2022 Istanbul bombing. Endorsement of binding moral foundations increased following the attack, yet this rise in group-oriented moral concerns did not translate into greater prosocial behavior. Generosity decreased from pre to post, and experimentally heightening the threat reduced cooperation. Changes in individualizing foundations followed an ideology-related pattern, with larger declines among conservative individuals, revealing a culture-specific ideological asymmetry in reactions to threat. Our study challenges the generalizability of terror-response models developed in Western societies and highlights the need for cross-cultural research on morality and behavior.
